extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy outlines Humana's national drug code (NDC) billing requirements.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. The following policy applies to professional and facility claims, except inpatient facility claims. The NDC is the industry standard for identifying the specific drug administered. Reporting the NDC enables accurate and timely claims adjudication. Other than the exceptions outlined in this policy, Humana requires a provider to report an accurate, valid NDC with a Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) drug code. Humana denies a HCPCS drug code submitted without an NDC. A denied HCPCS drug code that requires an NDC can be resubmitted with an NDC, within timely filing guidelines, for reconsideration of payment. To eliminate the need to try to determine whether an NDC would be required in a specific scenario, Humana strongly encourages providers to submit each HCPCS drug code with the accurate, valid corresponding NDC.

reimbursement_guidelines.title: Reimbursement Guidelines
reimbursement_guidelines.content:
In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. The following policy applies to professional and facility claims, except inpatient facility claims. The NDC is the industry standard for identifying the specific drug administered. Reporting the NDC enables accurate and timely claims adjudication. Other than the exceptions outlined in this policy, Humana requires a provider to report an accurate, valid NDC with a Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) drug code. Humana denies a HCPCS drug code submitted without an NDC. A denied HCPCS drug code that requires an NDC can be resubmitted with an NDC, within timely filing guidelines, for reconsideration of payment. To eliminate the need to try to determine whether an NDC would be required in a specific scenario, Humana strongly encourages providers to submit each HCPCS drug code with the accurate, valid corresponding NDC.

An NDC is not required with the following:

Child and adult immunization drug codes;

Gene therapy drug codes;

Radiopharmaceutical drug codes.

Humana requires the following when reporting an NDC:

For CMS-1500 paper claims: Report the NDC qualifier N4 followed by the 11-digit NDC in box 24.

For UB-04 paper claims: Report the NDC qualifier N4 followed by the 11-digit NDC in box 43.

For electronic claims: Report the NDC in loop 2410. Report NDC qualifier N4 in segment LIN 02 and the NDC in segment LIN 03.

When using different vial sizes that share the same HCPCS drug code but have different NDCs, for the same patient, bill multiple lines in order to report each unique NDC.

Report the NDC in a 5-4-2 digit format. If necessary, add a zero, as indicated in the examples below.

Do not report dashes, as indicated in the examples below.

3333-4444-55 03333-4444-55 03333444455

33333-444-55 33333-0444-55 33333044455

33333-4444-5 33333-4444-05 33333444405

In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana Medicaid plans require a provider to submit a HCPCS drug code charge with an accurate, valid corresponding NDC according to applicable state Medicaid agency requirements.
